title: The Citadel, Jerusalem. A Summary of Work since 1934
author: C. N. Johns
location_note: The Citadel (el-Qal'a) by the Jaffa Gate, Jerusalem; no map reference; placed by name.
reading: pp. 121-123 in full; then every paragraph with an eligible-class keyword, with the drain, stepped tank, quarry pit, burial and cistern passages read in full (pp. 138-139, 147, 152-153, 158, 162, 175, 179, 185, 188-190)
notes: Final summary of the Citadel excavations 1934-48: first to fourth builds of the city wall and towers (Early Hellenistic or Maccabean to Herodian), Roman legionary cantonment after AD 70, Byzantine-Islamic deposits, Crusader, Mamluk and Turkish castle. Walls and towers not eligible. A dry-stone corbelled chamber with access shaft (p. 147), function not given, is not coded. Cisterns of Ophel and Bishop Gobat School are cited comparisons, not coded. The full title is taken from the article heading as printed in the issue; the contents line reads 'The Citadel, Jerusalem'.
